articles.hausa_translation: Jiya, 'yan sanda sun yarda cewa mayakin nasu ne suka harbi mai kafantawa da ake kira Stone, kuma suka bayar da dalili. Jama'a da yawa suka tashi hannu a cikin zanga-zanga akan wannan abin ciki a jihar Enugu.
critical_questions: What specific justification did police give for shooting Stone, and is it independently corroborated or only from the police account?
Why were Anti-Cultism operatives the ones responding, and does this indicate potential profiling or assumptions made about Stone before engagement?
How many witness accounts from youths or community members are included versus official police statements, and whose narrative dominates?
What evidence exists for or against Stone being involved in cultism, and was lethal force truly necessary?
Why was this incident significant enough to trigger mass protests—does it reflect broader patterns of police violence in Enugu that warrant investigation?

articles.title: DRC begins new vaccine trial as outbreak kills over 4,600
articles.summary:
The trial, named Tumaini, which means “hope” in Swahili, will assess vaccine candidates designed to protect against the Bundibugyo virus, for which no vaccine has been approved
The post DRC begins new vaccine trial as outbreak kills over 4,600 appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria.
articles.hausa_translation: DRC yana fara sabuwar gwaje-gwajen allurar rigakafi kamar yadda cutarwar Bundibugyo ta kashe mutane sama da 4,600
critical_questions: What is the mortality rate and case count trajectory - is the outbreak still accelerating or declining, and how does this compare to previous Bundibugyo outbreaks?
Who are the funding sources and pharmaceutical companies behind the Tumaini trial, and do they stand to profit from vaccine approval?
Why was no vaccine previously developed for Bundibugyo despite historical outbreaks, and what changed to prioritize this now?
Are affected communities in the DRC being adequately informed and consenting to trial participation, or are vulnerable populations being enrolled without proper safeguards?
What containment measures are currently deployed alongside the trial - is the vaccine trial being positioned as a substitute for proven outbreak control methods?

articles.title: Okpebholo vows to sign death warrant against convicted kidnappers after 30 days
articles.summary:
The Edo governor said insecurity was a major concern when he assumed office but decided to prioritise tackling it, after raising the issue with President Bola Tinubu, who urged him to go ahead.
The post Okpebholo vows to sign death warrant against convicted kidnappers after 30 days appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria.
articles.hausa_translation: Okpebholo ya yi alkawari na sa hannu ga hukuncin mataki-mataki ga masu kidnapping da aka yanke hukunci bayan kwanaki 30
critical_questions: What is the evidentiary basis for executing convicted kidnappers, and how many cases will actually meet the legal threshold for capital punishment?
Why does the governor need presidential approval to pursue state-level security policy, and what specific constraints or incentives did President Tinubu's endorsement impose?
Who are the 'convicted kidnappers' currently in custody, and has there been transparent judicial review of these cases by civil society or international observers?
How does signing death warrants address the root causes of kidnapping (poverty, governance gaps, criminal networks), or is this primarily a symbolic political gesture?
Whose voices are missing—families of kidnapping victims, legal experts on deterrence, death row inmates' representatives—and why is this framed as a unilateral executive action?

articles.summary: Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has reacted to the deployment of security operatives to guard posters and billboards of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Kaduna ahead of his planned visit on Saturday. Daily Trust had reported how security personnel were stationed at strategic locations across the metropolis to prevent possible […]

critical_questions: What is the actual security threat that justifies deploying operatives to guard billboards rather than protecting citizens?

What evidence exists that security personnel were 'stationed' to guard posters versus normal campaign security protocols?
Are opposition figures receiving equal security resources for their campaign materials, or is this a selective enforcement issue?

Why is the story sourced only from NEMA's dashboard—where are independent verification, survivor testimonies, or state government perspectives?
